{{dablink|For other uses of the word "Bili," see [[Bili]].}}

'''''Bili Under the Hill''''' is a children's book about a hero named Bili.{{ref/book|4|6}} He went searching for gold and received three answers. The next day, he found that ten years had passed and he possessed a bag that was always full of gold.{{ref/book|4|8}}{{ref/book|twotc|Bili Under the Hill}}

==Background==
[[Elayne Trakand]] is reminded of the story when [[Moiraine Damodred]] tells her about the [[twisted redstone doorframe]] ''[[ter'angreal]]'' in the [[Stone of Tear]] that one may enter to get three true answers to three questions.{{ref/book|4|6}} [[Matrim Cauthon]] is reminded of the tale when [[Egwene al'Vere]] tells him the story.{{ref/book|4|8}} After Mat exits the twisted red doorway, he worries that they will go back upstairs to find ten years gone like Bili in the story.{{ref/book|4|15}} [[Tuon]] references the three answers when she asks if Mat believes that if you sleep on [[Caisen Hob|Old Hob's]] Hill under a full moon, the [[Eelfinn|foxes]] will give you true answers to three questions, or that [[Aelfinn|snakes]] steal people's skins and take the nourishment from food so you can starve to death while eating your fill.{{ref/book|11|10}} The story appears to be a reference to the victims of the [[Aelfinn]] and [[Eelfinn]].

==Parallels==
Bili's story has parallels with {{Wlink|lotr|Bilbo Baggins}} of Tolkien's ''{{Wiki|The Hobbit}}'', who lived under a hill and had many underground adventures, including playing three rounds of a riddle game with Gollum, and returning home with a massive quantity of gold.

The story also parallels the titular character of {{Wiki|Rip Van Winkle}}, who after a nap in the mountains discovered twenty years had passed, as well as various legends of adventurers exploring prehistoric mounds who unwittingly enter Faerie worlds and return to find many years have elapsed.
